newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela gov't may raise minimum salary - source.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela gov't may raise minimum salary - source.

text.p: The Venezuelan government is considering a January increase in the minimum monthly salary, top government sources said on Friday.
"The government is aware of the situation faced by workers and their loss of purchasing power," one source said. "In January something will be done to correct this."
What is being contemplated is "a general wage increase for all (public) employees," to be extended to the private sector.
With inflation now running at an annual rate of 114 percent, the powerful Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV) has pressed the government for months to grant an across-the-board wage increase.
The government source said the rise might take the form of bonuses being integrated into wages.

Through bonuses and other benefits, the minimum take-home income for civil servants was increased in February to 40,000 bolivars ($85 at the current exchange rate). Payment of a further one-time bonus is still pending.
For the private sector, the minimum income was raised in March to 52,000 bolivars ($112).
According to central bank figures, Venezuelan wages dropped 53 percent in real terms between 1988 and 1995.
